For it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and a song of praise is fitting.<sup>2</sup>The LORD builds up Jerusalem; he gathers the outcasts of Israel.<sup>3</sup>He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.<sup>4</sup>He determines the number of the stars; he gives to all of them their names.<sup>5</sup>Great is our Lord, and abundant in power; his understanding is beyond measure.<sup>6</sup>The LORD lifts up the humble; he casts the wicked to the ground.<sup>7</sup>Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make melody to our God on the lyre!<sup>8</sup>He covers the heavens with clouds; he prepares rain for the earth; he makes grass grow on the hills.<sup>9</sup>He gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens that cry.<sup>10</sup>His delight is not in the strength of the horse, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man,<sup>11</sup>but the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his steadfast love.<sup>12</sup>Praise the LORD, O Jerusalem! Praise your God, O Zion!<sup>13</sup>For he strengthens the bars of your gates; he blesses your children within you.<sup>14</sup>He makes peace in your borders; he fills you with the finest of the wheat.<sup>15</sup>He sends out his command to the earth; his word runs swiftly.<sup>16</sup>He gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes.<sup>17</sup>He hurls down his crystals of ice like crumbs; who can stand before his cold?<sup>18</sup>He sends out his word, and melts them; he makes his wind blow and the waters flow.<sup>19</sup>He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and rules to Israel.<sup>20</sup>He has not dealt thus with any other nation; they do not know his rules. Praise the LORD!

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–6 — He Determines the Number of the Stars
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise the LORD! For it is good to sing praises to our God (v. 1). The LORD builds up Jerusalem; he gathers the outcasts of Israel (v. 2). He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds. He determines the number of the stars; he gives to all of them their names (vv. 3-4). The LORD lifts up the humble (v. 6).
verseByVerse.theology: The God who counts and names the stars bends down to bandage broken hearts.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD! For it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and a song of praise is fitting. The LORD builds up Jerusalem; he gathers the outcasts of Israel. He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise the LORD! For it is good to sing praises to our God; for it is pleasant, and a song of praise is fitting.

Three reasons to praise, all about praise itself. It is good — right. It is pleasant — enjoyable (the ESV notes it may be "for he is beautiful"). And it is fitting — appropriate, the natural response to who God is. Praise is not an unnatural duty; it is what a creature was made for.

The LORD builds up Jerusalem; he gathers the outcasts of Israel.

A city rebuilt, and people who had been scattered and cast out brought home. Very likely the psalm celebrates the return from exile and the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. God is a builder of ruins and a gatherer of outcasts.

He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds.

And then, at once, the most personal kind of healing. The brokenhearted — people crushed by grief, betrayal, loss. God heals them, and binds up their wounds, like a nurse carefully wrapping a bandage. God does not only rebuild cities. He tends individual wounds.

verseByVerse.quote: He determines the number of the stars; he gives to all of them their names. Great is our Lord, and abundant in power; his understanding is beyond measure. The LORD lifts up the humble; he casts the wicked to the ground.
verseByVerse.commentary:
He determines the number of the stars; he gives to all of them their names.

And now the psalm does something breathtaking. Straight after the bandages, it looks up at the night sky. The God who binds up broken hearts is the God who determines the number of the stars — billions upon billions, beyond counting — and gives to all of them their names. Isaiah said, Lift up your eyes on high and see: who created these? He who brings out their host by number, calling them all by name (Isa 40:26).

Put verses 3 and 4 side by side. The same God. The one who knows every star by name knows your broken heart, and stoops to bandage it. His greatness does not make him too big to care; it makes his care unlimited. Jesus said, even the hairs of your head are all numbered (Matt 10:30).

Great is our Lord, and abundant in power; his understanding is beyond measure. The LORD lifts up the humble; he casts the wicked to the ground.

Beyond measure — literally without number, the same word used of the stars in verse 4: his understanding cannot be counted. And he uses his power to lift up the humble (the ESV notes afflicted) and bring down the wicked.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 7–11 — The LORD Takes Pleasure in Those Who Fear Him
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving (v. 7). He covers the heavens with clouds, sends rain, makes grass grow, and feeds the young ravens that cry (vv. 8-9). His delight is not in the strength of the horse (v. 10), but the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his steadfast love (v. 11).
verseByVerse.theology: God feeds the ravens and is not impressed by strength — he delights in those who hope in his love.

verseByVerse.quote: Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make melody to our God on the lyre! He covers the heavens with clouds; he prepares rain for the earth; he makes grass grow on the hills. He gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens that cry.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving; make melody to our God on the lyre!

A second call to praise, and a second set of reasons.

He covers the heavens with clouds; he prepares rain for the earth; he makes grass grow on the hills. He gives to the beasts their food, and to the young ravens that cry.

Clouds, rain, grass, food — the whole cycle of provision. And a detail that is easy to miss: the young ravens that cry. Ravens were unclean birds, scavengers, of no value to anyone. Their chicks squawk in the nest. God hears them and feeds them. Jesus made the same point: your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not of more value than they? (Matt 6:26). If God answers the cry of a raven chick, he will hear yours.

verseByVerse.quote: His delight is not in the strength of the horse, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man, but the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his steadfast love.
verseByVerse.commentary:
His delight is not in the strength of the horse, nor his pleasure in the legs of a man,

The horse was the ancient war machine — speed, power, military might. The legs of a man — the runner, the athlete, the soldier's strength. These are what the world admires. God is not impressed. Strength, speed and power do not delight him.

but the LORD takes pleasure in those who fear him, in those who hope in his steadfast love.

What does delight him? Those who fear him — who take him seriously. And those who hope in his steadfast love — who have given up relying on their own strength and are waiting on his love.

That is a great comfort for anyone who feels weak, slow, unimpressive. God does not take pleasure in the strongest or fastest. He takes pleasure in the one who hopes in him. The weakest believer who trusts God's love delights God more than the mightiest army.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 12–20 — He Declares His Word to Jacob
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise the LORD, O Jerusalem! (v. 12). He strengthens her gates, blesses her children, gives peace and the finest wheat (vv. 13-14). He sends out his command to the earth; his word runs swiftly (v. 15): snow, frost, ice — and he sends out his word, and melts them (vv. 16-18). He declares his word to Jacob; He has not dealt thus with any other nation (vv. 19-20).
verseByVerse.theology: The same word that sends the snow and melts it has been spoken to God's people — a privilege no other nation had.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD, O Jerusalem! Praise your God, O Zion! For he strengthens the bars of your gates; he blesses your children within you. He makes peace in your borders; he fills you with the finest of the wheat.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise the LORD, O Jerusalem! Praise your God, O Zion! For he strengthens the bars of your gates; he blesses your children within you.

A third call to praise, now to the city. The rebuilt gates are strong, their bars secure — and inside them, children, blessed. A city with safe walls and children in its streets is a city at peace.

He makes peace in your borders; he fills you with the finest of the wheat.

Peace at the borders, and the best bread — the finest of the wheat, the gift God longed to give his people in Psalm 81 if only they would listen (81:16). Here they have it.

verseByVerse.quote: He sends out his command to the earth; his word runs swiftly. He gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes. He hurls down his crystals of ice like crumbs; who can stand before his cold? He sends out his word, and melts them; he makes his wind blow and the waters flow.
verseByVerse.commentary:
He sends out his command to the earth; his word runs swiftly.

Now the word of God is pictured as a runner, racing across the earth to carry out his command.

He gives snow like wool; he scatters frost like ashes. He hurls down his crystals of ice like crumbs; who can stand before his cold?

And what the word does: winter. Snow falling like soft white wool. Frost scattered over the ground like grey ash. Hail and ice crystals thrown down like crumbs. Who can stand before his cold? Anyone who has been in a hard winter feels the force of that question. God speaks, and to the snow he says, Fall on the earth (Job 37:6).

He sends out his word, and melts them; he makes his wind blow and the waters flow.

And then — the same word — thaw. He speaks again, and the ice melts, the wind turns warm, and frozen streams start to flow. The word that brought the winter ends it. For a believer in a frozen season of life, that is a hopeful thing to know: the same God who sent the cold can send the word that melts it.

verseByVerse.quote: He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and rules to Israel. He has not dealt thus with any other nation; they do not know his rules. Praise the LORD!
verseByVerse.commentary:
He declares his word to Jacob, his statutes and rules to Israel.

And here is the climax. The word that commands the snow has been spoken, in words, to a people. His statutes and rules (the ESV notes just decrees) — his law, his revelation — given to Israel.

He has not dealt thus with any other nation; they do not know his rules. Praise the LORD!

This is a staggering privilege. Every nation receives snow and rain; only Israel had received God's revealed word. Moses asked, what great nation is there, that has statutes and rules so righteous as all this law? (Deut 4:8). Paul said the chief advantage of the Jews was that the Jews were entrusted with the oracles of God (Rom 3:2).

And now that word has gone out beyond Israel. The risen Christ sent his disciples to make disciples of all nations (Matt 28:19). If you have a Bible in your language, you hold the privilege this psalm celebrates. God has spoken to you — the same God who names the stars and melts the ice. Praise the LORD!

147.title: He Heals the Brokenhearted
147.overview: Praise is good, pleasant and fitting (v. 1). The LORD rebuilds Jerusalem and gathers its outcasts, heals the brokenhearted and binds their wounds, and numbers and names the stars; he is great, with understanding beyond measure, lifting the humble and casting down the wicked (vv. 2-6). Sing to him, who sends clouds and rain, makes grass grow, and feeds animals and crying young ravens; he delights not in the horse's strength or a man's legs but in those who fear him and hope in his steadfast love (vv. 7-11). Let Jerusalem praise him: he strengthens her gates, blesses her children, gives peace and the finest wheat (vv. 12-14). His word sends snow, frost and ice, and his word melts them (vv. 15-18). He has declared his word to Israel as to no other nation. Praise the LORD (vv. 19-20).
147.theology:
Praise is fitting for creatures (v. 1). The God who numbers and names the stars heals individual broken hearts (vv. 3-4; Isa 40:26; Matt 10:30), and cares for the least creatures (v. 9; Matt 6:26).

God delights not in human strength but in those who fear him and hope in his love (vv. 10-11). His word governs creation, sending and ending winter (vv. 15-18; Job 37:6).

The supreme gift is God's revealed word, given first to Israel (vv. 19-20; Deut 4:7-8; Rom 3:2) and now sent to all nations (Matt 28:19).
147.examples:
A nurse wrapping a bandage.

The God who names the stars knows your broken heart.

Raven chicks squawking in the nest — heard.

God is not impressed by the fastest or the strongest.

Children safe inside strong gates.

Snow like wool, frost like ash.

The same word that sends the winter ends it.

A Bible in your language: the privilege of Jacob.

148.text: <sup>1</sup>Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights!<sup>2</sup>Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts!<sup>3</sup>Praise him, sun and moon, praise him, all you shining stars!<sup>4</sup>Praise him, you highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens!<sup>5</sup>Let them praise the name of the LORD! For he commanded and they were created.<sup>6</sup>And he established them forever and ever; he gave a decree, and it shall not pass away.<sup>7</sup>Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all deeps,<sup>8</sup>fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind fulfilling his word!<sup>9</sup>Mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars!<sup>10</sup>Beasts and all livestock, creeping things and flying birds!<sup>11</sup>Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth!<sup>12</sup>Young men and maidens together, old men and children!<sup>13</sup>Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his majesty is above earth and heaven.<sup>14</sup>He has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his saints, for the people of Israel who are near to him. Praise the LORD!

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–6 — Praise the LORD from the Heavens
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights! (v. 1). Praise him, all his angels (v. 2); praise him, sun and moon, praise him, all you shining stars! (v. 3). Let them praise the name of the LORD! For he commanded and they were created (v. 5). He gave a decree, and it shall not pass away (v. 6).
verseByVerse.theology: Angels, stars and the highest heavens are summoned to praise the one who spoke them into being.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights! Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts! Praise him, sun and moon, praise him, all you shining stars! Praise him, you highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise the LORD! Praise the LORD from the heavens; praise him in the heights!

This psalm is a roll call of the whole universe. It has two great choirs. The first is in the heavens (vv. 1-6); the second is on the earth (vv. 7-14). Everything that exists is called by name and told to praise.

Praise him, all his angels; praise him, all his hosts!

First, the highest creatures: the angels, the armies of heaven. They already do it. Nehemiah prayed, the host of heaven worships you (Neh 9:6). The psalm joins its voice to theirs.

Praise him, sun and moon, praise him, all you shining stars! Praise him, you highest heavens, and you waters above the heavens!

Then the sky itself. The sun, which the nations worshipped as a god, is told to worship the LORD. The moon and all you shining stars — every one of them, the stars God numbers and names (147:4). The highest heavens, and the waters above the heavens, the waters God separated at creation. Nothing in the sky is too high to bow.

How can a star praise? Not with words. By shining as God made it to shine, by doing exactly what it was created for. Every star in its course is a note in the song.

verseByVerse.quote: Let them praise the name of the LORD! For he commanded and they were created. And he established them forever and ever; he gave a decree, and it shall not pass away.
verseByVerse.commentary:
Let them praise the name of the LORD! For he commanded and they were created.

And the reason the heavenly choir must praise: he commanded and they were created. They owe their existence to his word. A creature praises its Creator simply by acknowledging where it came from.

And he established them forever and ever; he gave a decree, and it shall not pass away.

And he keeps them there. The laws that govern the sky — the orbits, the seasons, the rising sun — are his decree, and it shall not pass away (the ESV notes it may be "it shall not be transgressed"). The regularity of the universe is the faithfulness of God.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 7–14 — Praise the LORD from the Earth
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all deeps (v. 7), fire, hail, snow and wind, mountains, trees, beasts and birds (vv. 8-10), kings of the earth and all peoples, young men and maidens together, old men and children! (vv. 11-12). Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted (v. 13). He has raised up a horn for his people (v. 14).
verseByVerse.theology: From the sea monsters to the smallest child, all earth joins the choir, and God's own people most of all.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all deeps, fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind fulfilling his word! Mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars! Beasts and all livestock, creeping things and flying birds!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise the LORD from the earth, you great sea creatures and all deeps,

Now the earthly choir, and it starts at the bottom: the depths of the sea and the great sea creatures — the monsters of the deep, the whales, the things sailors feared. Even they praise.

fire and hail, snow and mist, stormy wind fulfilling his word!

Then the weather — lightning, hail, snow, fog, and the stormy wind fulfilling his word. The previous psalm showed God's word sending the snow and melting it (147:15-18). Here the storms praise him by obeying.

Mountains and all hills, fruit trees and all cedars! Beasts and all livestock, creeping things and flying birds!

Then the land: mountains and hills, orchards and forests; wild animals and farm animals; the things that crawl and the things that fly. The list almost follows the order of creation. Everything God made on the earth is summoned to the choir.

verseByVerse.quote: Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth! Young men and maidens together, old men and children!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Kings of the earth and all peoples, princes and all rulers of the earth!

And finally humanity, and it starts with the most powerful: kings, princes, rulers. They are not exempt. The mightiest human being is called to bow and praise with the birds and the cattle.

Young men and maidens together, old men and children!

And then everyone else, paired across every difference: young men and young women; the elderly and the children. No age, no sex, no rank is left out. A little child singing to God and an old man singing to God are in the same choir as the sun and the angels.

John saw this choir complete: every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea, and all that is in them, saying, To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and might forever and ever! (Rev 5:13). When the crowds praised Jesus on the road into Jerusalem and the Pharisees told him to silence them, he said, if these were silent, the very stones would cry out (Luke 19:40).

verseByVerse.quote: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his majesty is above earth and heaven. He has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his saints, for the people of Israel who are near to him. Praise the LORD!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Let them praise the name of the LORD, for his name alone is exalted; his majesty is above earth and heaven.

The earthly choir ends with the same line as the heavenly one: Let them praise the name of the LORD (compare v. 5). And the reason: his name alone is exalted. Not the sun's, not the king's. His majesty is above earth and heaven — above both choirs.

He has raised up a horn for his people, praise for all his saints, for the people of Israel who are near to him. Praise the LORD!

And the psalm ends by narrowing from the whole universe to one people. Of all the creatures that praise God, one group has a special reason. God has raised up a horn for his people — strength, a deliverer, the horn God promised to make sprout for David (132:17). Zechariah sang when Christ was coming: God has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David (Luke 1:69).

And they are the people ... who are near to him. The stars praise from far away. God's people praise from close up. Paul tells Gentile believers, you who once were far off have been brought near by the blood of Christ (Eph 2:13). All creation sings; the redeemed sing nearest.

148.title: Praise Him, Sun and Moon
148.overview: Praise the LORD from the heavens: angels, hosts, sun, moon, stars, the highest heavens and the waters above them, for he commanded and they were created and established by his unchanging decree (vv. 1-6). Praise him from the earth: sea creatures and deeps, fire, hail, snow, mist and storm, mountains, trees, animals and birds, kings, princes and all peoples, young and old (vv. 7-12). Let them praise his name, which alone is exalted above earth and heaven; he has raised up a horn for his people Israel, who are near to him (vv. 13-14).
148.theology:
All creation, in heaven and on earth, is called to praise its Creator (vv. 1-12; Neh 9:6; Rev 5:13); creatures praise by being and doing what God made them for. His word created them and sustains their order (vv. 5-6, 8).

Human rank and age give no exemption (vv. 11-12). God's name alone is exalted (v. 13).

His own people have a unique reason and nearness: the horn of salvation he has raised up (v. 14; 132:17; Luke 1:69), and they are brought near to him (Eph 2:13).
148.examples:
A roll call of the universe.

The sun, worshipped by nations, told to worship.

A star praises by shining as it was made to.

Storms praising by obeying.

Kings in the same choir as the cattle.

An old man and a child, singing with the angels.

The stars praise from far off; the redeemed from close up.

149.text: <sup>1</sup>Praise the LORD! Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the godly!<sup>2</sup>Let Israel be glad in his Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King!<sup>3</sup>Let them praise his name with dancing, making melody to him with tambourine and lyre!<sup>4</sup>For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation.<sup>5</sup>Let the godly exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.<sup>6</sup>Let the high praises of God be in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands,<sup>7</sup>to execute vengeance on the nations and punishments on the peoples,<sup>8</sup>to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron,<sup>9</sup>to execute on them the judgment written! This is honor for all his godly ones. Praise the LORD!

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–5 — The LORD Takes Pleasure in His People
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise the LORD! Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the godly! (v. 1). Let Israel be glad in his Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King! (v. 2), with dancing, tambourine and lyre (v. 3). For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation (v. 4). Let them sing for joy on their beds (v. 5).
verseByVerse.theology: God's people dance and sing because their King takes pleasure in them.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD! Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the godly! Let Israel be glad in his Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King! Let them praise his name with dancing, making melody to him with tambourine and lyre!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise the LORD! Sing to the LORD a new song, his praise in the assembly of the godly!

After the whole universe was summoned to praise in Psalm 148, this psalm brings the focus to God's gathered people — the assembly of the godly. And they sing a new song, because God has done something new for them.

Let Israel be glad in his Maker; let the children of Zion rejoice in their King!

Two titles for God, and two relationships. He is Israel's Maker — he formed them as a people. And he is their King — he rules them. The people are glad in both. They are not ashamed of the one who made them or resentful of the one who rules them. They rejoice.

Let them praise his name with dancing, making melody to him with tambourine and lyre!

Dancing, drums and strings. Worship in the Psalms is not always solemn. When God has saved his people, joy may be loud and physical. Miriam took a tambourine and danced at the Red Sea; David danced before the ark.

verseByVerse.quote: For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation. Let the godly exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.
verseByVerse.commentary:
For the LORD takes pleasure in his people; he adorns the humble with salvation.

Here is the reason for all the joy, and it is astonishing. The LORD takes pleasure in his people. Not merely tolerates them, puts up with them, or uses them. He delights in them. Zephaniah said the same: he will rejoice over you with gladness; he will quiet you by his love; he will exult over you with loud singing (Zeph 3:17). God's people sing over God, and God sings over his people.

And he adorns the humble with salvation. Salvation is pictured as beautiful clothing or jewellery, and it is given to the humble — not the proud, not the self-sufficient, but those who know their need. God dresses the lowly in splendour.

If you have ever thought that God merely endures you, read this verse again. He takes pleasure in his people.

Let the godly exult in glory; let them sing for joy on their beds.

Joy that follows them home. Not only in the assembly, but on their beds at night — lying awake, not with worry, but singing. The bed that was once a place of tears in so many psalms has become a place of praise.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 6–9 — This Is Honor for All His Godly Ones
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Let the high praises of God be in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands, to execute vengeance on the nations (vv. 6-7), to bind their kings with chains (v. 8), to execute on them the judgment written! This is honor for all his godly ones. Praise the LORD! (v. 9).
verseByVerse.theology: Praise and judgment belong together — and for the church, the sword is the word, and the judgment is Christ's.

verseByVerse.quote: Let the high praises of God be in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands, to execute vengeance on the nations and punishments on the peoples, to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron, to execute on them the judgment written! This is honor for all his godly ones. Praise the LORD!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Let the high praises of God be in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands,

And now a verse that has to be read with great care. Praise in the throat — and a two-edged sword in the hand. Worship and warfare together.

to execute vengeance on the nations and punishments on the peoples, to bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron, to execute on them the judgment written! This is honor for all his godly ones. Praise the LORD!

In its first setting, this was Israel as God's army, carrying out the judgments God had pronounced — the judgment written — against nations that opposed him. It was not private revenge, and it was not unlimited; it was God's sentence, already written, carried out under his command.

This text has been badly misused. People have quoted it to bless wars, crusades and violence done in God's name. That is a grave mistake. The New Testament tells Christians exactly how to read it.

First, the church's warfare is not with physical weapons: the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh but have divine power to destroy strongholds (2 Cor 10:4). The Christian's sword is the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God (Eph 6:17) — and God's word is sharper than any two-edged sword (Heb 4:12). The high praises of God and the preaching of his word go out together, and they bring down strongholds of unbelief.

Second, the final judgment of the nations belongs to Christ himself. John saw him: From his mouth comes a sharp sword with which to strike down the nations (Rev 19:15). The sword comes from his mouth — his word. And believers will share in that judgment only as he shares it with them: the saints will judge the world (1 Cor 6:2). Until then, never avenge yourselves (Rom 12:19).

So this is honor for all his godly ones: to praise God with full throats, to carry his word like a two-edged sword into a world in rebellion, and to share one day in the victory of the King who takes pleasure in them. Praise the LORD!

149.title: A New Song in the Assembly of the Godly
149.overview: A new song is to be sung in the assembly of the godly; Israel is to be glad in its Maker and King, praising him with dancing, tambourine and lyre (vv. 1-3). The LORD takes pleasure in his people and adorns the humble with salvation; let them exult and sing on their beds (vv. 4-5). With God's high praises in their throats and two-edged swords in their hands, they are to carry out the written judgment on the nations and bind their kings; this is the honour of the godly. Praise the LORD (vv. 6-9).
149.theology:
God's people rejoice in their Maker and King (v. 2), and God takes pleasure in them, clothing the humble with salvation (v. 4; Zeph 3:17).

Praise and the execution of God's written judgment belong together (vv. 6-9). For the church the sword is the word of God (2 Cor 10:4; Eph 6:17; Heb 4:12), the final judgment is Christ's (Rev 19:15), shared by the saints only at his appointment (1 Cor 6:2), and personal vengeance is forbidden (Rom 12:19). The text gives no warrant for violence in God's name.
149.examples:
Glad in the one who made them and the one who rules them.

Dancing before the King.

God does not merely endure his people; he delights in them.

Salvation worn like jewellery by the humble.

The bed of tears turned into a bed of song.

A text misused for war, rightly read as the word.

The sword that comes from Christ's mouth.

150.text: <sup>1</sup>Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in his mighty heavens!<sup>2</sup>Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his excellent greatness!<sup>3</sup>Praise him with trumpet sound; praise him with lute and harp!<sup>4</sup>Praise him with tambourine and dance; praise him with strings and pipe!<sup>5</sup>Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with loud clashing cymbals!<sup>6</sup>Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 1–2 — Praise God in His Sanctuary
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in his mighty heavens! (v. 1). Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his excellent greatness! (v. 2).
verseByVerse.theology: Where to praise and why: everywhere God is, for everything he has done and is.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in his mighty heavens!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise the LORD! Praise God in his sanctuary; praise him in his mighty heavens!

This is the last psalm, and it contains nothing but praise. No lament, no request, no enemies, no questions. In six verses the word praise comes thirteen times. The Psalter, which has walked through every human experience — guilt, grief, fear, exile, betrayal, doubt, joy — ends here.

And the first thing it says is where. In his sanctuary — the temple on earth, where God's people gather. And in his mighty heavens — the ESV notes the Hebrew is expanse, the word used for the sky God made on the second day of creation. Praise on earth and praise in heaven. The two choirs of Psalm 148, joined.

There is no place where praise is out of place, because there is no place where God is not.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his excellent greatness!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise him for his mighty deeds; praise him according to his excellent greatness!

Then why. Two reasons, and they cover everything. For his mighty deeds — what God has done: creation, the exodus, the return from exile, every rescue in every psalm before this one. And according to his excellent greatness — who God is. Praise is to match his greatness, and since his greatness has no limit, praise never reaches its end.

The whole Psalter has been a record of these two things: the deeds of God and the greatness of God. Psalm 150 simply gathers them up and says: praise him for all of it.

verseByVerse.ref: vv. 3–6 — Let Everything That Has Breath
verseByVerse.sectionOverview: Praise him with trumpet sound; praise him with lute and harp! (v. 3). Praise him with tambourine and dance; praise him with strings and pipe! (v. 4). Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with loud clashing cymbals! (v. 5). Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD! (v. 6).
verseByVerse.theology: Every instrument, and then every living thing: the book of Psalms ends in one great shout of praise.

verseByVerse.quote: Praise him with trumpet sound; praise him with lute and harp! Praise him with tambourine and dance; praise him with strings and pipe! Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with loud clashing cymbals!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Praise him with trumpet sound; praise him with lute and harp! Praise him with tambourine and dance; praise him with strings and pipe! Praise him with sounding cymbals; praise him with loud clashing cymbals!

Now how. And the answer is: with everything. The trumpet — the ram's horn blown by the priests, the sound of festivals and coronations. The lute and harp — the strings of the Levite musicians. The tambourine and dance — the joy of ordinary people, the women with Miriam at the sea. Strings and pipe — shepherds' instruments. And then the cymbals, twice: sounding, and loud clashing.

The list moves from the priests' instruments to the people's, and from the quiet to the loud. Every kind of music in Israel is enlisted. When Solomon's temple was dedicated, when the song was raised, with trumpets and cymbals and other musical instruments, in praise to the LORD, For he is good, for his steadfast love endures forever, the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud (2 Chr 5:13). God filled the house with his glory while the music played.

The psalm is not laying down a rule about which instruments churches must use. It is saying that nothing is too loud, too joyful or too ordinary to be offered to God in praise. Paul calls Christians to psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody to the Lord with your heart (Eph 5:19). The heart is the instrument that matters most.

verseByVerse.quote: Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!
verseByVerse.commentary:
Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!

And finally, who. Not only the priests, not only Israel, not only the musicians. Everything that has breath.

Think of what breath has meant in these psalms. When you take away their breath, they die and return to their dust (104:29). When his breath departs, he returns to the earth (146:4). Breath is God's gift, lent to every living creature, and it will be taken back. The last verse of the Psalms says what that borrowed breath is for: to praise the one who gave it. Every breath you take is on loan from God, and it was given to you to be returned as praise.

The book of Psalms began, Blessed is the man who walks not in the counsel of the wicked (1:1) — a blessing, and a choice between two ways. It ends with every breathing thing praising the LORD. Between those two verses lie a hundred and fifty psalms of tears and trust, sin and forgiveness, exile and homecoming. And the destination of it all is praise.

John saw that destination reached. Every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea was singing To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honor and glory and might forever and ever! (Rev 5:13). And he heard what seemed to be the voice of a great multitude, like the roar of many waters, crying, Hallelujah! For the Lord our God the Almighty reigns (Rev 19:6). For from him and through him and to him are all things. To him be glory forever. Amen (Rom 11:36).

If you have breath, you are included in this last verse. Praise the LORD!

150.title: Let Everything That Has Breath Praise the LORD
150.overview: The final psalm calls for praise of God in his sanctuary and in the expanse of heaven (v. 1), for his mighty deeds and surpassing greatness (v. 2), with trumpet, lute, harp, tambourine, dance, strings, pipe and cymbals (vv. 3-5). Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD! (v. 6).
150.theology:
The Psalter ends in pure praise, answering where (heaven and earth, v. 1), why (God's deeds and greatness, v. 2), how (every kind of music and the whole heart, vv. 3-5; 2 Chr 5:13; Eph 5:19), and who (everything that has breath, v. 6).

Breath is God's gift to every creature (104:29-30; 146:4), given to be returned in praise. The book that begins with the blessed man's choice of ways (1:1) ends with universal praise, fulfilled in the song of all creation to God and the Lamb (Rev 5:13; 19:6). All things are from him, through him and to him (Rom 11:36).
150.examples:
Thirteen praises in six verses, and nothing else.

No place where praise is out of place.

Praise that must match a greatness without limit.

The priests' trumpet and the people's tambourine.

Cymbals, twice — the loudest last.

Borrowed breath, returned as praise.

From Blessed is the man to Praise the LORD!

If you have breath, you are in the last verse.
